plan_a_advantages: More focused speed work (tempo runs) for pace improvement.
Dedicated strength training session to build leg power and stability.
Incorporates cross-training to maintain aerobic fitness without excessive impact.
plan_b_advantages: Includes more long runs, which can be beneficial for building overall endurance.
Hill session provides a specific strength stimulus, though less targeted than Plan A’s strength work.
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates more targeted speed work (tempo runs) and a dedicated strength training session, both crucial for improving running pace and efficiency on trails. Plan B, while including hill work, relies heavily on longer, predominantly easy-paced runs, which, while building endurance, won't directly translate to faster times. Plan A’s structured approach to building both aerobic base and specific speed capabilities is more aligned with the goal of becoming a faster trail runner. Furthermore, the inclusion of a dedicated strength session addresses a common weakness in trail runners – leg strength – which is vital for tackling technical terrain.
